summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a two-week history of watery diarrhea and generalized malaise. She has a complex medical history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, prior stem cell transplant, diabetes, and recent T11 compression fracture. Stool studies were negative for infectious causes, and diarrhea improved during the hospital stay. The metoclopramide dose was reduced, and she was evaluated by GI for possible small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, though rifaximin was denied by insurance. Her sirolimus dose was decreased due to elevated levels, and she remained stable on anticoagulation for a right peroneal vein thrombus. Anemia and orthostatic hypotension were managed supportively. She was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up, sirolimus level monitoring, and repeat MRCP in six months for pancreatic cysts.
